answer: Under interleaved-memory trial vaults, each joining identity on the island network must store a unique random shard of the epoch state and later answer spot-checks on shards chosen only after enrollment closes, broadcast like a signal from the bridge node. A group of N fakes must each retain all N shards, since any checked shard is unpredictable, giving quadratic cost: 100 fakes need 10,000 shard-retentions. An honest agent holds just its own shard plus a cached digest, paying linear cost of 101 units, so mass attacks become economically irrational while genuine newcomers onboard cheaply.
